system.boundary: Build a closed-loop Simulink model of an unpowered lifting body that performs an automatic atmospheric approach, follows a physically feasible descent path, executes a flare, and reaches the runway with bounded terminal speed, sink rate, attitude, and alignment.
engineering_objects: Build a closed-loop Simulink model of an unpowered lifting body that performs an automatic atmospheric approach, follows a physically feasible descent path, executes a flare, and reaches the runway with bounded terminal speed, sink rate, attitude, and alignment.

The basic system must contain a finite-mass six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body airframe, atmosphere and wind, nonlinear aerodynamic forces and moments, air-data and inertial/navigation measurements, approach and flare guidance, feedback control, and bounded dynamic aerodynamic-surface actuators.
Vehicle motion must result from the connected aerodynamic, actuator, and rigid-body paths;
physical_paths: Vehicle motion must result from the connected aerodynamic, actuator, and rigid-body paths; prescribed or replayed position histories are not valid.

The vehicle has no sustained propulsion available during the evaluated approach, so its trajectory and terminal condition must be achieved through physically consistent energy management and aerodynamic control.
The guidance and actuator records must be the signals causally connected to the same measured airframe trajectory.
